proposal:
read_data_into_fd: Fix spurious "Seek error" when appending to a non-empty file

Since 3.8.8, extracting into a non-empty file opened for appending fails, although the data is written:

```
$ echo header > out
$ bsdtar -xOf t.tar f >> out
f: Seek error: Unknown error -1
bsdtar: Error exit delayed from previous errors
$ echo $?
1
```

`bsdcat f.gz >> out` fails the same way, and `bsdtar -xO` stops after the first entry.
The final check from #3128 compares how far the descriptor offset moved with the bytes written, but with O_APPEND the first write moves the offset to the end of the file.

Following stoeckmann's suggestion, archive_read_data_into_fd() no longer seeks over holes when the descriptor is not a regular file or was opened with O_APPEND. Holes are written as zeros, so the check holds and sparse entries append correctly too.

test_read_data_into_fd_append appends two plain entries and a sparse one to a non-empty file. It fails without the fix with "Seek error" and passes with it. On Windows it runs with its own expected output, because WriteFile() ignores the CRT's O_APPEND. The suite passes in an ASan and UBSan build.

proposal: fix: apply emphasis flanking and rules 9-10 to the whole delimiter run **Marked version:** 18.1.1 (master at 6dd5b3c) **Markdown flavor:** CommonMark (GitHub Flavored Markdown output is the same for these inputs) ## Description No existing issue. Below is the issue in the template's format. ## Expectation Emphasis should follow CommonMark 0.31.2 (6.2, rules 9 and 10). Flanking and the "multiple of 3" rule look at the whole delimiter run that holds the opener. The rule also applies when the opener can close as well as open, not only when the closer can open. Expected output is what commonmark.js 0.31.2 gives: | input | commonmark.js | marked 18.1.1 | |---|---|---| | `***.a*` | `**.a` | `***.a*` | | `**(a)*` | `*(a)` | `**(a)*` | | `foo ***!bar*` | `foo **!bar` | `foo ***!bar*` | | `a*b**` | `a*b**` | `ab*` | | `x a*b** y` | `x a*b** y` | `x ab* y` | | `__(_*` | `__(_*` | `_(*` | ## Result There are two causes, both in `emStrong`. 1. When the whole run can't close, the lexer takes its first delimiter as text and tries the rest again. On that retry `prevChar` is the delimiter itself (`*`). The `punctuation` rule leaves out `*` and `_`, so if the run is followed by punctuation (`**(a)*`) the left-flanking check fails, and the shorter opener never gets tried. For `_` the retry keeps the right `prevChar`, but rules 9-10 then count only what is left of the run (`__(_*` gives 1 + 1 rather than 2 + 1). 2. Rules 9-10 were only applied when the closer could open (`match[5]`/`match[6]`), never when the opener could close. In `a*b**` the `*` is both left- and right-flanking, so 1 + 2 is a multiple of 3 and it must not pair with `**`. ## What was attempted `emStrong` now walks back through `maskedSrc` to the start of the current run. Masking keeps the length, and escaped delimiters are masked as `+`, so a run of delimiter characters there is the real run. The character before the run is used for the flanking check on a mid-run retry. The full run length is used for rules 9-10. That same character tells us whether the opener can also close; when it can, rules 9-10 apply to closers that can only close too. The other delimiter character (`_` before `**`) counts as punctuation for that check, as it does in CommonMark. Pedantic mode is not changed, since markdown.pl has none of these rules. The existing mid-run guard from #4008 (`**a*b*c`) is kept and now runs before the rule 9-10 check. ## Contributor - [x] Test(s) exist to ensure functionality and minimize regression (if no tests added, list tests covering this PR); or, - [ ] no tests required for this PR. - [ ] If submitting new feature, it has been documented in the appropriate places. Before, the inner text was wrong on its own (`****(**` stayed literal), and that happened to hide the problem.
